title: Jailer Tops Tamil Films in North America as Jailer 2 Enters Top Ten
excerpt: Koimoi's all-time ranking puts Jailer at $7.25 million and Coolie at $6.95 million in North America, with Jailer 2 entering at No. 7 — and a reporting caveat that explains why rival tallies differ.
body:
• Rajinikanth's Jailer leads the all-time Tamil list in North America at $7.25 million, ahead of Coolie at $6.95 million and Ponniyin Selvan 1 at $6.7 million, according to Koimoi's updated ranking.
  • Rajinikanth accounts for six of the top 10 titles; Vijay accounts for two (Leo and The Greatest Of All Time) and Mani Ratnam's Ponniyin Selvan films account for two.
  • Jailer 2 enters the ranking at No. 7 with $5.17 million — a ranking story, separate from the sequel's daily box-office run.
  • For diaspora readers, the numbers come with a caveat: Koimoi says its figures are estimates, and Canada collections for Tamil films have historically been under-reported, so rival tallies differ.

The all-time North America chart for Tamil cinema is, by a wide margin, a Rajinikanth chart. Koimoi's updated ranking of the highest-grossing Kollywood films in North America — the United States and Canada combined — puts Jailer first at $7.25 million, followed by Coolie at $6.95 million and Mani Ratnam's Ponniyin Selvan 1 at $6.7 million.

The newest entry is Jailer 2, at No. 7 with $5.17 million. That placement, rather than any single day's collection, is the story: a sequel released five years after streaming reshaped overseas viewing still drew enough theatrical business in the US and Canada to pass Kabali and every Tamil release except six titles.

Why the tallies argue with each other

North America totals for Tamil films are contested in a way domestic Indian totals rarely are. When Sun Pictures announced that Coolie had become the all-time highest-grossing Tamil film in North America at $6,719,999, the claim sat awkwardly next to Jailer's earlier run. MovieCrow's breakdown of that dispute explains the mechanics: North America is treated as a single territory, Comscore — the industry-standard tracking source — does not break out Canada separately unless a distributor requests and pays for it, and Canadian collections for Tamil films have long gone unreported when they were at or below $1.5 million, because smaller local partners handled distribution there.

On MovieCrow's accounting, which adds estimated Canadian grosses back in, Jailer reached $7.27 million and 2.0 reached an estimated $7.5 million — a different ordering from Koimoi's reported-gross table. Readers should treat the Koimoi list as the ranking of reported collections, not as an audited ledger. The full explainer is at MovieCrow.

How the leaders got there

The top of the chart was built on opening weekends. Coolie, directed by Lokesh Kanagaraj, grossed $3.04 million on its premiere day in North America — the highest premiere-day figure for a Tamil film — after becoming the fastest Tamil film to cross $3 million in the USA and drawing more than 100 crore rupees in worldwide advance bookings, Cinema Express reported, citing Sun Pictures. That front-loaded pattern is now the overseas model for star-led Tamil releases: premieres and the first weekend decide the ranking, and the long tail decides little.

The composition of the list tells its own story. Six Rajinikanth titles — Jailer, Coolie, 2 Point 0, Jailer 2, Kabali and Enthiran — span 2010 to the present, which means the North America market for Tamil cinema has been anchored by one star across three decades of his career. Vijay's Leo at No. 4 and The Greatest Of All Time at No. 9 are the only non-Rajinikanth star vehicles in the ten, and the two Ponniyin Selvan films are the only literary epics.

What it means for the diaspora market

For exhibitors in New Jersey, Texas, California, Ontario and other Tamil diaspora centres, the practical reading is that a top-tier Tamil opening is now a $5 million-plus North America proposition, and only a handful of names can deliver it. That concentration shapes screen allocation, premiere pricing and how early distributors lock screens.

What's next

The next test of the chart is whether any non-Rajinikanth, non-Vijay release can break the $5 million line that now separates the top seven from the rest. Until a new star vehicle does, Jailer's $7.25 million remains the number every Tamil opening weekend in North America is measured against.
